issue_context.title: Migrate hack/verify-featuregates.sh and hack/update-featuregates.sh to golangci-lint plugin architecture
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Recently in #125830 (as part of https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4330) a `static analysis script to verify new feature gates are added as versioned feature specs` was added to the code base that uses a bespoke linter setup.   This approach is temporary/alpha with the desired approach for beta of the https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4330 using a golangci-lint plugin (see https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125830#issuecomment-2260449394)

### Why is this needed?

From comments on the initial PR https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/125830#issuecomment-2260449394 and some associated user issues/friction posted after this change (https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126741#issuecomment-2293634664) it makes sense to migrate the current bespoke linter script and go code to instead be a golangci-lint plugin to address.  Doing so is identified as a must-do before  https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/issues/4330 can move to `beta` (mentioned in the above PR comment as future work) and the bug here tracks that work.  Reasons the golangci-lint plugin approach is preferred is:

- more performance (golangci-lint caching, etc)
- in line with kubernetes/kubernetes linting best practices
- removes need for `update-features` concept and helps with source of truth issues seen currently
comments: I'm curious if we really need to maintain a full fledged featuregate checker in the next release. Assuming that we port all the feature gates over and they're all versioned, there will be no examples of unversioned feature gates in the code. Do we even still need a linter to make sure that all features are versioned?

> Do we even still need a linter to make sure that all features are versioned?

unless you are completely sure there can not be unversioned fetures gates in the code is always possible for someone to add them back without being noticed ... so we can not depend on human to review and make sure this policy is applied, we need to rely on machines to ensure this can not happen 🤖  :)

Okay let's keep this issue open until we can confirm whether all features can be ported to versioned. My instinct says yes but we'll need the actual PRs, opened a tracking issue for all the features here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/126926

> I'm curious if we really need to maintain a full fledged featuregate checker in the next release. Assuming that we port all the feature gates over and they're all versioned, there will be no examples of unversioned feature gates in the code. Do we even still need a linter to make sure that all features are versioned?

I would like to maintain a static analysis checker so that we can output [this file](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/command-line-tools-reference/feature-gates/) instead of manually maintaining it by hand. It would be possible by post-processing output as we do for [instrumentation documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/metrics/).

We have agreed to keep the tool separate based on the constraints here: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129414#issuecomment-2711743310

In doing so we've renamed the tool to make it clear that it is not a general purpose analysis tool and added documentation.

See: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/129414

review_comments: I just noticed that `defaultKubernetesFeatureGates` is empty. Wouldn't it be possible to remove it and this line then?
This one for unittest is still have value. But I think we can remove the one in pkg/features and staging/src/apiserver/pkg/features now?

If it has no effect in production code, then it shouldn't be in the production code.

If it still matters somehow for unit tests, then those tests can set it up.
Sounds good. I created https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/130121 to update them.
